title: Whose Language Counts as High Quality? Measuring Language Ideologies in Text Data Selection

bias_targets.methodology: Applying the GPT-3 quality filter to U.S. high school newspaper articles to evaluate how automated text filtering disproportionately excludes specific stylistic features (e.g., first/second person pronouns) and non-professional/non-hegemonic topics.
Regressing the GPT-3 quality filter scores of high school newspaper articles against the median home values of the schools' corresponding ZIP codes.
Correlating the assigned quality filter scores of school newspapers with the percentage of the county population living in rural versus urban areas.
Analyzing the relationship between document quality scores and the percentage of adults with at least a bachelor's degree in the school's ZIP code.
Evaluating the correlation between the school newspapers' average quality scores and the 2016 Republican (GOP) presidential vote share at the county level.
Regressing text quality scores against the racial demographics of the school's student body (e.g., percentage of Asian, Black, and Hispanic students) as a control variable check.
